definitions.explanation: A complex structure of interconnecting passages that is difficult to navigate, whether real or fictional.
Figuratively, a situation — especially a criminal investigation — that has become so complicated it seems impossible to solve. Used in the expression 迷宮入り.

examples.japanese: {地下|ちか}の{迷宮|めいきゅう}を{探検|たんけん}する。
このダンジョンは{巨大|きょだい}な{迷宮|めいきゅう}になっている。
examples.english: This dungeon is an enormous maze.

examples.japanese: ギリシャ{神話|しんわ}のクレタ{島|とう}の{迷宮|めいきゅう}には{恐|おそ}ろしいミノタウロスが{住|す}んでいたとされる。
examples.english: According to Greek mythology, the fearsome Minotaur dwelled in the labyrinth on the island of Crete.

examples.japanese: この{事件|じけん}は{迷宮入|めいきゅうい}りした。
{手|て}がかりがなく、{捜査|そうさ}は{迷宮|めいきゅう}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: With no leads, the investigation hit a dead end.

examples.japanese: {発生|はっせい}から{二十年|にじゅうねん}が{経|た}ち、{迷宮入|めいきゅうい}りしていた{殺人事件|さつじんじけん}にようやく{進展|しんてん}があった。
examples.english: Twenty years after the crime occurred, there was finally progress in the murder case that had gone cold.

notes:
Compound of {迷|めい} (to be lost) + {宮|きゅう} (palace, building).

KEY EXPRESSION:
{迷宮入|めいきゅうい}り — when a criminal case goes cold or becomes unsolvable. This is one of the most common uses in news and detective fiction.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {迷宮入|めいきゅうい}りする (to go cold, become unsolvable)
- {迷宮|めいきゅう}のような (labyrinthine)
- {迷宮|めいきゅう}を{彷徨|さまよ}う (to wander a maze)

USAGE:
In gaming and fantasy contexts, {迷宮|めいきゅう} is commonly used for "dungeon" or "labyrinth." In crime reporting, {迷宮入|めいきゅうい}り is the standard term for a cold case.
